newsitem.title: INDIA: Crosby sees India liquidity tightening by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Crosby sees India liquidity tightening by year-end.

text.p: Crosby Securities said on Wednesday it expected credit creation by Indian banks to pick up in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) on the back of an industrial revival.
It forecast a tightening of liquidity by December 1996.
In its September South Asia Economic Review, Crosby said the revival of credit combined with government borrowing would increase Indian demand for funds.
"The supply of funds will not increase proportionately because broad money supply growth will be reined in at 15.3 percent in 1996/97 (April-March)," it said.
"Excess demand for funds will, therefore, lead to a tightening of liquidity by December 1996," it said. "Short-term interest rates will then move back to current levels."
But Crosby said the liquidity squeeze was unlikely to be as severe as the one experienced in the second half of 1995/96.
